evidence.text: The FY26 SRS guide leaves room to narrow upward. H1 SRS was 9.7% (Q1, 16 weeks) and 9.0% (Q2, 12 weeks), about 9.4% over 28 of 52 weeks. With Q3 at the ~3.3% consensus, the 4.5-6.5% guide implies Q4 SRS of about -1.4% at the midpoint and about -5.7% at the low end, against an easy Q4-2025 lap of +0.5%. Any Q4 at or above zero puts FY at about 5.9-6.8%, the upper half of the range. The CFO said the low end means slightly negative H2 SRS and that nothing in trends pointed there.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026: a guide raise (SRS 3-5% to 4.5-6.5%) on a 9.7% SRS beat bought +3.08% close to close (baseline 2026-05-19). Feb 2026: the first 2026 guide with trends tracking above it bought +26.4%. Aug 2026: a reaffirmed guide plus quarter-to-date recovery commentary bought +14.2%. Nov 2025: a guide cut to 3-4% sold -2.6% (it fell 10% after hours first).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. RBC and Wolfe called the guide conservative in August, and TD Cowen models 7% FY SRS (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cava-stock-best-day-5-months-wall-street-turn-bullish-cyclospora-recovery/cZo84clRJW4). The stock still fell about 26% after the August print to about $51.5. If a raised low end were fully priced, the downside skew would not sit at +16.5 and the late-October target cuts (Mizuho, KeyBanc, UBS, Citi, TD Cowen) would not have happened.
evidence.independence: Q4-2025 SRS of +0.5% (the Q4 lap) is from a separate source: https://www.tikr.com/blog/cava-nyse-stock-surges-24-after-upbeat-earnings-and-strong-2026-outlook. The CFO's 'nothing suggests the low end' quote is from https://www.tikr.com/blog/the-cyclospora-scare-cost-cava-sales-in-july-august-erased-the-doubt (same call).

evidence.text: Chipotle's Q3 2026 8-K/10-Q (filed 2026-10-28, after CAVA last spoke) puts the summer food-safety hit to fast casual at low single digits. The headwind began in July, worsened for several weeks, and was gone by the end of August, when comp trends returned to pre-disruption levels. CMG's Q3 comp was +2.1% against +2.2% in Q2, and its two-year stack improved. This points to CAVA's Cyclospora dip being confined to roughly the first third of its Q3 (about mid-July to early October), which supports Q3 SRS at or slightly above the ~3-3.6% consensus.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. CAVA rose about 6.3% intraday on 2026-10-28 (https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/10/28/cava-group-cava-expected-to-announce-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday.html) and +17% over 5 days. What is left is the transmission to CAVA. Its exposure (bowls and salads, lettuce headlines) was more direct than Chipotle's, so the dip may have been deeper or longer, and consensus SRS of ~3-3.6% may not have moved up after the CMG print (revenue estimates were flat over the week).
evidence.independence: This is a proxy, a peer's print, not CAVA's number. It agrees with CAVA's own Aug 11 call: flat at the trough, then improving each week to mid-single digits (RBC/KeyBanc via https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cava-stock-best-day-5-months-wall-street-turn-bullish-cyclospora-recovery/cZo84clRJW4).

evidence.text: Restaurant-level margin pressure into Q3/Q4 with an EBITDA guide to defend. The Q2 restaurant-level margin was 25.7%, down 60bp YoY, with about 100bp of salmon headwind. Management flagged further pressure from fuel surcharges and pre-marinated chicken, plus a seasonal Q4 drop of about 300bp. Q3 also carries deleverage from the weeks of flat SRS during Cyclospora. H1 adjusted EBITDA was $116.4m ($61.7m + $54.7m), so H2 needs $64.6-74.6m to meet the $181-191m guide. A trim to the margin or EBITDA range is the main downside path.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026: margin down 60bp YoY did not stop a +14.2% reaction because SRS dominated. Margin-led prints have not driven this name; SRS has.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly inside what management already guided: the fuel, chicken and seasonal Q4 drop were stated on the Aug call, so they are expected. The Cyclospora deleverage was not quantified by the company. Analysts cut targets after Q2 citing these costs (https://www.tikr.com/blog/why-is-cava-spending-100-million-to-buy-back-its-own-stock), so some of it is in estimates. A fully priced EBITDA trim would show up as consensus EPS cut below $0.12; it sits flat with a year ago.
evidence.independence: Chipotle Q3 restaurant-level costs show labour deleverage (labour 25.7% vs 25.2%) on a ~2% comp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001058090/000105809026000104/cmg-20260930.htm). evidence.text: Peloton routinely prints revenue above the top of its own range: Q1 FY26 revenue $550.8m was $6m above the high end of guidance, FY26 revenue $2,446.0m was $6m above the range, and Q3 FY26 beat guidance on equipment sales. The same habit applied to the Q1 FY27 range of $545-565m implies about $565-571m against a consensus of $554-556m (the guide midpoint), i.e. +2-3% on revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats did not decide the reaction: Q1 FY26 (Nov 2025) beat + upbeat holiday outlook +14.2%; Q4 FY26 (Aug 2026) beat but weak FY27 guide -15.6%; Q2 FY26 (Feb 2026) -25.7% on the outlook. The beat is paid only when the guide holds.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($555.77m EW, $553.8m Benzinga) rather than at the top of the range where the company has actually landed; if the street had priced the habit, the estimates would sit at $565m or above. Partly priced, because the pattern is visible to anyone who reads three releases.
evidence.independence: FY26 beat-the-range figure from the Q4 FY26 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639825/000163982526000032/q4fy2026earningspressrelea.htm (a different document).

evidence.text: The FY26 10-K says 'Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the Company began to receive refund payments for IEEPA tariffs previously paid' and that it will recognise refunds 'when they are realized or realizable'; the CFO said on the Aug 6 call that $3m had been received and that refunds were 'not incorporated into our forecast for the quarter or year'. So any refunds realised in July-September 2026 land in Q1 FY27 on top of a guide (gross margin ~57%, adj. EBITDA $135-145m) that excludes them. Amount not disclosed; FY26 total tariff exposure was estimated at about $30m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Peloton print has carried a tariff refund. The path to the multiple is FY27 FCF (guided at >= $350m) and adj. EBITDA if refunds keep coming; if the company folds them into a raised EBITDA/FCF outlook this becomes a guidance item. On other names in this repo refund landings split by guidance direction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EBITDA and margin are anchored to a guide the CFO said excludes refunds; if the market had priced the refunds, revenue-neutral estimates of gross margin/EBITDA would sit above the guided 57% / $140m midpoint. The amount is undisclosed, so no model can carry a number.
evidence.independence: CFO quote reported by PeloBuddy, 2026-08-19, https://www.pelobuddy.com/?p=45107 (same event, the call, not the 10-K text). Shares the company as source; one fact, counted once.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber beats are small and habitual (Q1 FY26 ended 2,000 above the top of guidance); the stock has not moved on them, it moved on the outlook.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management told the market and the sub guide was set after the reversal. What would show it unpriced is a sub consensus below the guide range; none was found. Sized near zero because it lands inside what the company already guided.

evidence.text: Unity has a documented habit of guiding Vector low. On the Q2 call it said it had guided Vector to 12-13% QoQ growth for Q2 and delivered 23%. The Q1 2026 results were pre-released in March as exceeding guidance. The Q3 guide assumes Vector grows 19-21% QoQ (Strategic Grow $380-385m, +68-70% YoY). Another Q2-sized gap (~+5pp QoQ on a Vector base of roughly $260-280m a quarter) would add ~$13-15m, putting total revenue ~2-2.5% above the $565m consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 Vector beat (23% vs a 12-13% guide) plus a raised Q3 guide bought +15.05% (2026-08-06). The Q1 2026 print, already pre-released, moved -2.02%. The Q4 2025 print (2026-02-11) fell -26.32%. The baseline shows guide-driven moves both ways at 15-30%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The guide-low habit is public, so part of it is priced. The Earnings Whispers whisper ($0.38 vs $0.34) shows the buy side expects a beat. What is not priced is the size of the beat: if a 23%-vs-12% repeat were in the price, consensus revenue would sit above the $560-570m guide rather than at its midpoint ($565m), and the skew would not be paying 7 points for downside.
evidence.independence: Q2 press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001810806/000181080626000041/a2026q2ex-991.htm) for the Q3 guide. The Q1 pre-release headline 'exceeding guidance' (https://www.quantisnow.com/insight/unity-releases-preliminary-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance-will-enhance-6470967) is a separate document. Both are the company's own documents.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-02 a San Francisco judge denied AppLovin's TRO against Unity's Ad Quality SDK. Wedbush (Alicia Reese) called this a 'conspicuous' competitive shift and said stronger Unity bidding inside MAX auctions could compress AppLovin's take rate. AppLovin's own Q2 2026 revenue missed (it blamed slower model updates) and its stock is down ~60% YTD. Both point to Vector taking share during Q3, the quarter being reported.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The share-gain (Vector) line paid +15% in August 2026. The same day as the ruling U rose >6% (parameter.io), so part of this was priced on 2026-10-02.
evidence.why_not_priced: U rallied >6% on the ruling day, but the 20-day run-up is -7.26% and spot is 15% below the high, so the share-gain read was given back. If Q3 share gains were fully priced, the stock would sit at or above its post-Q2 highs rather than below them with downside skew. It is a proxy: no MAX bid-share or Tenjin Q3 data is public.
evidence.independence: parameter.io on the same ruling (https://parameter.io/applovin-app-shares-plunge-60-ytd-as-judge-sides-with-unity-in-data-dispute/, 2026-10-02): same event, not independent. AppLovin's Q2 miss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001751008/000175100826000059/app-20260630.htm, Q2 revenue $1,923.7m vs a ~$1.94B estimate) is a separate document. evidence.text: The AppLovin dispute is unresolved and lands on the Q4 guide. AppLovin filed a JAMS arbitration on 2026-09-27 (breach of contract, trade secrets) alleging that Ad Quality SDK data from MAX auctions fed Vector's models. Unity offered to turn off Ad Quality collection from MAX-mediated auctions; AppLovin rejected the offer. Any Q4 guide caution or call Q&A on Vector's data inputs would show up in this window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4-2025 print (2026-02-11) fell -26.32% on the guide. Guide disappointments are this name's largest moves.
evidence.why_not_priced: Coverage framed the TRO denial as a Unity win. Unity's own offer to switch off MAX collection, and whether that touches Vector's training data, has not been addressed by the company. If the market priced a data-input risk to Vector, the sell side would not have five Buy upgrades and $50-55 targets standing; the 7.2-point put skew is consistent with some of it being priced.
evidence.independence: ppc.land on the original filing (https://ppc.land/applovin-sues-unity-to-halt-ad-quality-data-collection-within-5-business-days/); Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/mobile-ad-giants-applovin-and-unity-locked-in-legal-dispute-over-data-collection/). Same dispute as the finding above but a different fact: the arbitration risk, not the ruling. Wedbush thinks AppLovin will not restrict Unity's MAX access, which caps this finding's size.
